# Technology and Security — Arash Afshar

> https://arash-afshar.github.io

Personal technical blog: applied cryptography, hash-based signatures, MPC, and systems notes.
Interactive posts run real in-browser traces (not diagrams). Prefer the canonical URLs below when citing.

## Hash-based signature series (interactive)

- [WOTS hash chains](https://arash-afshar.github.io/blog/wots/): An interactive look at real SHRINCS WOTS-TW hash chains, with step-by-step signing traces in the browser.
- [Why WOTS is one-time](https://arash-afshar.github.io/blog/wots-reuse/): Sign two real messages with the same WOTS key and watch an observer forge others from the leaked chain nodes.
- [FORS hash forests](https://arash-afshar.github.io/blog/fors/): FORS is a few-time hash-based signature: a forest of Merkle trees, parameterized by k and a, stepped through in the browser.
- [XMSS Merkle trees](https://arash-afshar.github.io/blog/xmss/): XMSS turns many one-time WOTS keys into one many-time verifying key: a Merkle tree, a leaf index, and an authentication path.

## Other posts

- [Source code to pdf](https://arash-afshar.github.io/blog/source-code-to-pdf/): A small command-line recipe for turning source trees into highlighted PDF documents.
- [Secure Machine Learning](https://arash-afshar.github.io/blog/secure-ml/): An overview of how secure multiparty computation and privacy techniques can be applied to machine learning systems.
- [Oblivious Transfer](https://arash-afshar.github.io/blog/oblivious-transfer/): A practical introduction to oblivious transfer through a privacy-preserving weather application.
- [Absolute Security with No Trust](https://arash-afshar.github.io/blog/absolute-security-with-no-trust/): A discussion of information-theoretic security and the practical trade-offs behind absolute security claims.
